summary: @servicetitan/anvil-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is written with hex-mangled identifiers and per-function property-bag objects that obscure ordinary strings (fs/https imports, URLs, argv, process names). It downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/..., extracts the archive to a temporary directory, marks the bun binary executable, and then invokes that freshly-downloaded runtime against a bundled file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB file bearing a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header and a large string-array/opcode table with a rotation function characteristic of a bytecode-VM obfuscator — its name and contents do not correspond to anything in a React component library. Executing an obfuscated bundled payload via a just-downloaded alternate runtime at install time is an alternate-runtime dropper pattern that evades Node-based static review; the true behavior of math_init.js cannot be recovered from source. This is not a legitimate build step for a React UI library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
